The '''2011–12 season''' was '''[[FC Barcelona]]'s''' 113th in existence and the club's [[La Liga#All-time La Liga table|81st consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football. Barcelona debuted their new and first paid shirt sponsor [[Qatar Foundation]] after an agreement was reached in 2010 with the [[non-profit organization]] for a five-and-a-half-year, €170 million deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/castellano/noticies/club/temporada10-11/12/13/n101213114565.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20110923232643/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/castellano/noticies/club/temporada10-11/12/13/n101213114565.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 September 2011|title=Barça reach shirt sponsorship agreement with Qatar Foundation|language=es|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=13 December 2010|access-date=26 May 2011}}</ref> The agreement with [[UNICEF]] continued and their name had been moved to the lower back portion of the shirt.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://shop.fcbarcelona.com/stores/barcelona/products/product_maxzoom.aspx?maximage=prd_maxzoom_barca-86264.jpg&intPID=86264|title=Barcelona 2011-12 shirts|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=17 May 2011|access-date=26 May 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110520230132/http://shop.fcbarcelona.com/stores/barcelona/products/product_maxzoom.aspx?maximage=prd_maxzoom_barca-86264.jpg&intPID=86264|archive-date=20 May 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>
This season also introduced a new away kit in black while the third kit was retained from [[2010–11 FC Barcelona season|last season]].

Barcelona were unable to defend two major trophies: they finished as runners-up in Liga, nine points behind winners [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], who finished with a record 100 points,<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/05/02/real-madrid-beats-bilbao-la-liga-title-barcelona_n_1472847.html | title = Real Madrid Win La Liga Title With 3-0 Victory Over Athletic Bilbao | author = [[HuffPost]]| website = [[HuffPost]] | date = 2 May 2012 | access-date = 27 May 2012 }}</ref> and their [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] campaign ended after a 3–2 aggregate defeat in the semi-finals to eventual winners [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/champions-league/1-2-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_chelsea|title=Barça exit the CL.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=24 April 2012|access-date=2012-05-02}}</ref> [[Pep Guardiola]] stepped down as head coach at the conclusion of the season, which ended on a high as Barcelona beat [[Athletic Bilbao]] 3–0 in the [[2012 Copa del Rey Final|Copa del Rey final]] at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium|Vicente Calderón]].

Barcelona's under-19 squad played in the inaugural tournament of the [[2011–12 NextGen series|NextGen series]]. After finishing first in their group during the group stage, they were eliminated by [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] in the quarter-finals of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fixtures, Results & Tables|url=http://www.nextgenseries.com/en/FixturesResultsTables|publisher=NextGen Series|access-date=6 March 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Barcelona 0 – 3 Ajax|url=http://www.nextgenseries.com/en/FixturesResultsTables/Results/Wed-08-02-12/Barcelona-vs-Ajax/Barcelona---Ajax|publisher=NextGen Series|access-date=6 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120221025341/http://www.nextgenseries.com/en/FixturesResultsTables/Results/Wed-08-02-12/Barcelona-vs-Ajax/Barcelona---Ajax|archive-date=21 February 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Season overview==

===May/June===
On 31 May, [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] confirmed it had exercised its right to purchase [[defender (association football)|defender]] [[Martín Cáceres]], who spent the [[2010–11 Sevilla FC season|2010–11 season]] on loan with the club from Barcelona. Barcelona received €4.10 million in compensation after making the loan permanent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada10-11/05/31/n110531117809.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120730095000/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada10-11/05/31/n110531117809.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 July 2012 |title=Cáceres makes permanent move to Sevilla |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=31 May 2011 |access-date=21 June 2011 }}</ref>

===July===
On 2 July, Barcelona parted ways with [[midfielder]] [[Víctor Sánchez (footballer, born 1987)|Víctor Sánchez]] after both parties agreed to rescind the player's contract. Sánchez made 14 appearances with the first team in the [[2007–08 FC Barcelona season|2007–2008]] and [[2008–09 FC Barcelona season|2008–2009]] seasons. He was loaned to [[Xerez CD|Xerez]] for the [[2009–10 FC Barcelona season|2009–10 season]] and at [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] for the [[2010–11 FC Barcelona season|2010–11 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/07/02/n110702118241.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120730141336/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/07/02/n110702118241.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 July 2012 |title=Sánchez leaves Barça |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2 July 2011 |access-date=2 July 2011 }}</ref>

On 4 July, defender [[Andreu Fontàs]] was promoted to the first team after spending the [[2010–11 FC Barcelona season|previous season]] filling in for an injured [[Eric Abidal]], who had been diagnosed with a liver tumour.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/07/04/n110704118272.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120731092615/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/07/04/n110704118272.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=31 July 2012|title=Fontàs promoted to 1st Team|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=4 July 2011|access-date=7 July 2011}}</ref>

On 21 July, Barcelona completed the transfer of [[Chile national football team|Chilean]] [[Winger (association football)|winger]] [[Alexis Sánchez]] from Italian club [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]]. The deal is for five years and the cost of the transfer is €26 million with variable cost of €11.5 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/07/21/n110614117999.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120801192643/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/07/21/n110614117999.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=1 August 2012|title=Barça sign Alexis Sánchez|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=21 July 2011|access-date=21 July 2011}}</ref>

On 22 July, Barcelona transferred [[La Masia]] graduate [[Bojan Krkić|Bojan]] to Italian outfit [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] for €10 million and the agreement includes an obligatory re-purchase clause to be exercised by Barcelona at the end of the 2012–13 season, for a cost of €13 million. Roma may override this re-purchase at this time by paying the club an additional €28 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/07/22/n110712118387.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120803184320/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/07/22/n110712118387.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=3 August 2012 |title=Bojan transferred to AS Roma |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=22 July 2011 |access-date=22 July 2011 }}</ref>

===August===
On 3 August, [[Portugal|Portuguese]] club [[Sporting Clube de Portugal|Sporting CP]] made official the signing of another Barcelona's La Masia graduate, winger [[Jeffrén Suárez|Jeffrén]], on a five-year deal. The transfer deal was worth €3.7 million and includes a €30 million buyout clause.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sporting.pt/Noticias/Futebol/Fut_Prof/notfutprof_futjeffrenaquisicao_030811_78816.asp|title=Jeffrén makes Sporting switch|publisher=Sporting.pt|language=pt|date=3 August 2011|access-date=3 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004132517/http://www.sporting.pt/Noticias/Futebol/Fut_Prof/notfutprof_futjeffrenaquisicao_030811_78816.asp|archive-date=4 October 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 4 August, Barcelona and [[Argentina|Argentine]] [[centre-back]] [[Gabriel Milito]] reached an agreement to terminate his contract after four years with the team. He then signed with Argentine club [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/08/04/n110804118663.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120731110228/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/08/04/n110804118663.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=31 July 2012|title=Milito allowed to depart|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=4 August 2011|access-date=4 August 2011}}</ref>

On 14 August, both Barcelona and English club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] announced on their respective official websites an agreement for the transfer of [[Spain national football team|Spanish international]] midfielder [[Cesc Fàbregas]]. The deal will cost Barcelona €29 million with €11 million in variables and end one of the longest transfer sagas in football.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/arsenal-agree-terms-with-barca-for-fabregas|title=Arsenal announces Fàbregas transfer.|publisher=Arsenal.com|date=14 August 2011|access-date=14 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006164919/http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/arsenal-agree-terms-with-barca-for-fabregas|archive-date=6 October 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/destacades/n110815118780.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130101062548/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/destacades/n110815118780.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=1 January 2013 |title=Barça finally get Fàbregas. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=14 August 2011 |access-date=14 August 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/cesc-barcelona/20110814dasdasftb_41/Tes|title=Fàbregas' transfer detailed.|publisher=AS.com|language=es|date=14 August 2011|access-date=14 August 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20110812/fc-barcelona/arsenal-cesc-barca-la-negociacion-mas-larga-del-mundo_54198935099.html|title=Transfer 4 years in the making.|work=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=14 August 2011|access-date=14 August 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/942813/arsenal-skipper-fabregas-finally-signs-for-barcelona?cc=5901|title=Transfer numbers.|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=15 August 2011|access-date=15 August 2011|archive-date=26 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026145642/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/942813/arsenal-skipper-fabregas-finally-signs-for-barcelona?cc=5901|url-status=dead}}</ref> On the same day, Barcelona and [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] kicked off the 2011–12 season with a 2–2 draw at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] in the [[2011 Supercopa de España|first leg]] of the 2011 Supercopa de España in front of a full house.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=330062&cc=5901|title=Draw to kick off the new season.|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=14 August 2011|access-date=14 August 2011|archive-date=26 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026143109/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=330062&cc=5901|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 17 August, Barcelona won the Supercopa de España with a thrilling 3–2 win and a 5–4 aggregate over rivals Real Madrid. The match ended with several [[Misconduct (association football)#Sending-off offences (red card)|sending offs]] for a brawl started after Barcelona players deemed a tackle by [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]] on Cesc Fàbregas to be dangerous play. [[David Villa]], [[Mesut Özil]] and Marcelo all received their marching orders after calm was restored. Real Madrid manager [[José Mourinho]] and Barça's assistant [[Tito Vilanova]] were also involved in a small physical altercation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/330063?cc=5901|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120723222238/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/330063?cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 July 2012|title=Barcelona 3-2 Real Madrid|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=17 August 2011|access-date=17 August 2011}}</ref> Goals from [[Andrés Iniesta]] and a brace, including the game winner, by [[Lionel Messi]] assured Barça started their season with a trophy by claiming their tenth Supercopa all time.

On 19 August, the [[Association of Spanish Footballers]] (AFE) went on strike due to unpaid wages for players in the top two divisions of Spanish football by clubs who have gone into financial administration. The AFE and [[Liga de Fútbol Profesional]] (LFP) have yet to agree on a guaranteed fund to protect players' wages in the event of their clubs being declared insolvent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/945843/la-liga-fixtures-postponed-by-strike?cc=5901|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102034007/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/945843/la-liga-fixtures-postponed-by-strike?cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 November 2012|title=La Liga strikes|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=19 August 2011|access-date=20 August 2011}}</ref> The strike forced Spanish league games scheduled for the weekend of 20 and 21 August, including Barcelona's season opener against [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], to be postponed.

On 25 August, Lionel Messi was voted the winner of the inaugural [[UEFA Best Player in Europe Award]] for the 2010–11 season over teammate [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]] and Real Madrid's [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0250-0c50f3bb01f8-2230f3d90345-1000--messi-wins-uefa-best-player-in-europe-award/|title=Messi wins inaugural UEFA Best Player in Europe Award.|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=25 August 2011|access-date=25 August 2011}}</ref>

On 26 August, Barcelona won the UEFA Super Cup with a 2–0 victory over Portuguese outfit [[FC Porto|Porto]] in [[Monaco]]. The victory gave Barça their [[List of UEFA Super Cup winners#Performances|fourth]] UEFA Super Cup trophy all time and saw Fàbregas score his first goal with a Barcelona shirt in the 88th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/supercopa_europa/final/jornada01/Barcelona_oporto/partit.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120802205203/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/supercopa_europa/final/jornada01/Barcelona_oporto/partit.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 August 2012|title=Barça wins UEFA Super Cup|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=26 August 2011|access-date=26 August 2011}}</ref>

===September===
On 10 September, back from the [[FIFA]] international break, Barcelona could only draw 2–2 with [[Real Sociedad]] at [[Anoeta Stadium|Anoeta]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/lliga/jornada03/Real_Sociedad_Barcelona/partit.html|title=Draw after the international break.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=10 September 2011|access-date=10 September 2011|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120710035847/http://fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/lliga/jornada03/Real_Sociedad_Barcelona/partit.html|archive-date=10 July 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Barça also lost Alexis Sánchez for approximately 6–8 weeks after the player tore his [[hamstring]] in his right leg after a tackle by Sociedad's [[Daniel Estrada Agirrezabalaga|Dani Estrada]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/09/10/n110910119161.html|title=Alexis injured.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=10 September 2011|access-date=10 September 2011|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120707235306/http://fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/09/10/n110910119161.html|archive-date=7 July 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 13 September, Barcelona opened their UEFA Champions League campaign with a 2–2<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/champions_league/primera_fase/jornada01/grup_H/Barcelona_Milan/partit.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120730235557/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/champions_league/primera_fase/jornada01/grup_H/Barcelona_Milan/partit.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=30 July 2012|title=Draw in 1st CL match.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=13 September 2011|access-date=13 September 2011}}</ref> draw against [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] at the [[Camp Nou]]. Midfielder Andrés Iniesta left in the 38th minute with a tore [[Biceps femoris muscle|femoral biceps]] on his left leg and will miss approximately a month.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/09/13/n110913119212.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120802195803/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/09/13/n110913119212.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 August 2012|title=Iniesta to miss a month.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=13 September 2011|access-date=13 September 2011}}</ref>

On 17 September, after two consecutive draws Barcelona trashed [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] 8–0 at Camp Nou. Lionel Messi scored a [[Hat-trick#Association football|hat-trick]] and lead Barça to their biggest win of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20110917/fc-barcelona/8-0-un-gran-barca-despeja-dudas-con-una-goleada-a-osasuna_54217247690.html|title=Barça humiliate Osasuna.|work=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=17 September 2011|access-date=18 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110923163702/http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20110917/fc-barcelona/8-0-un-gran-barca-despeja-dudas-con-una-goleada-a-osasuna_54217247690.html|archive-date=23 September 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> Osasuna coach [[José Luis Mendilibar]] stated, "we've caught them very angry due to their so-called mini-crisis,"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/09/17/futbol/equipos/osasuna/1316293662.html|title=Mendilibar speaks about the trashing.|work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=17 September 2011|access-date=18 September 2011}}</ref> while Barça's coach Pep Guardiola stated in regards to the ''mini-crisis'', "the day I see them not running, that their bellies are full, I'll sit here to tell you all [media]. When we play bad, believe me I'll come here and tell you all. But I did not have that sensation."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/09/17/futbol/equipos/barcelona/1316294998.html|title=Guardiola on the mini-crisis.|work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=17 September 2011|access-date=18 September 2011}}</ref>

On 28 September, Barcelona defeated [[FC BATE Borisov|BATE Borisov]] 0–5<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/champions_league/primera_fase/jornada02/grup_H/bate_Barcelona/partit.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120801200719/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/champions_league/primera_fase/jornada02/grup_H/bate_Barcelona/partit.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=1 August 2012|title=Barça notch their 1st Group H win.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=28 September 2011|access-date=28 September 2011}}</ref> at the [[Dynama Stadium (Minsk)|Dynama Stadium]] in their first meeting in Group H of the Champions League. Lionel Messi scored a brace and tied [[László Kubala]] for 2nd place on the [[List of FC Barcelona records and statistics#Players|all-time goals scoring list]] for Barcelona with 194 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/09/28/n110928119478.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120905053839/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/09/28/n110928119478.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 September 2012|title=Messi draws even with Kubala.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=28 September 2011|access-date=28 September 2011}}</ref>

===October===
On 2 October, Barcelona defeated [[Sporting de Gijón]] 0–1<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/lliga/jornada07/Sporting_Gijon_Barcelona/partit.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120802045650/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/lliga/jornada07/Sporting_Gijon_Barcelona/partit.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 August 2012 |title=Barça go top. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2 October 2011 |access-date=2 October 2011 }}</ref> at [[El Molinón]] to take over first place in La Liga's [[2011–12 La Liga#League table|standings]] for the first time this season. A lone goal by [[Adriano (footballer, born 1984)|Adriano]] was enough to see the team go top by goal difference over [[Levante UD|Levante]].

On 19 October, Barcelona notched its second Champions League victory of the season by defeating [[Czech Republic|Czech]] side [[FC Viktoria Plzeň|Viktoria Plzeň]] 2–0 at the Camp Nou.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0254-0d7d4750a558-a55af65b9918-1000--barcelona-flex-muscles-without-overwhelming-plzen/|title=Barça beat Plzeň.|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=19 October 2011|access-date=27 October 2011}}</ref>

On 22 October, Barça were held scoreless for the first time in the young season by a heroic performance from Sevilla goalkeeper [[Javi Varas]]. The match ended with a scoreless draw after Lionel Messi's penalty kick was saved by Varas in injury time. The match towards the end was marred by a small brawl between [[Frédéric Kanouté]] and Cesc Fàbregas as the latter took offense to Kanouté kicking the ball from the penalty spot after Messi had placed it to take the spot kick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323957?cc=5901|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120720165956/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323957?cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 July 2012|title=Barça 0-0 Sevilla.|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=22 October 2011|access-date=27 October 2011}}</ref> After the match, Fàbregas was accused of racially abusing Kanouté, which the player vehemently denied and at the end both players apologized over the incident by telephone.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/974017/barcelona%27s-cesc-fabregas-denies-racially-abusing-frederic-kanoute?cc=5901|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111026024235/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/974017/barcelona%27s-cesc-fabregas-denies-racially-abusing-frederic-kanoute?cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 October 2011|title=Fàbregas accused of racism.|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=23 October 2011|access-date=27 October 2011}}</ref>

On 25 October, Barcelona traveled to [[Estadio Nuevo Los Cármenes|Los Cármenes]] to take on [[Granada CF|Granada]] where they escaped with a 0–1 victory after a 33rd-minute goal from a free-kick by [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/lliga/jornada10/Granada_Barcelona/partit.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120729182013/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_11-12/arxiu_partits/lliga/jornada10/Granada_Barcelona/partit.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=29 July 2012 |title=Barça claim narrow win. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=25 October 2011 |access-date=27 October 2011 }}</ref> Barça also lost forward [[Pedro (footballer, born 1987)|Pedro]] for approximately three weeks due to strained tendons in his left ankle.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/10/26/n111026119959.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120909130448/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/10/26/n111026119959.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 September 2012|title=Pedro suffers ankle injury in Granada.|publisher=2011-10-26|access-date=27 October 2011}}</ref>

===November===
On 1 November, the 23-men shortlist for the [[FIFA Ballon d'Or|2011 FIFA Ballon d'Or]] was released with eight Barcelona—Eric Abidal, [[Dani Alves]], Cesc Fàbregas, Andrés Iniesta, Lionel Messi, [[Gerard Piqué]], [[David Villa]] and Xavi.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/11/01/n111101120063.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120731103032/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/11/01/n111101120063.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=31 July 2012|title=FIFA Ballon d'Or 2011.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=1 November 2011|access-date=2 November 2011}}</ref> Later that night, Barcelona defeated Viktoria Plzeň 0–4 in [[Prague]] at the [[Synot Tip Arena]] with a hat-trick by Messi and assured their progress into the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knock-out stage]]. With the three goals, he surpassed the 200-goal mark as a Barcelona player in Pep Guardiola's 200th game as first team manager.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/11/01/n111101120061.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120730062012/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/11/01/n111101120061.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=30 July 2012|title=Guardiola reaches 200 games.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=1 November 2011|access-date=2 November 2011}}</ref> Goalkeeper [[Víctor Valdés]] broke the team record for most minutes without conceding a goal at 877 consecutive minutes. He surpasses [[Miguel Reina]] record of 824 minutes set in the [[1972–73 La Liga|1972–73 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/11/01/n111101120076.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120731173612/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada11-12/11/01/n111101120076.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=31 July 2012|title=Valdés breaks team shutout record.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=1 November 2011|access-date=2 November 2011}}</ref>

On 9 November, the first leg of the Round of 16 of the Copa del Rey was moved up due to Barcelona's involvement in the [[2011 FIFA Club World Cup]] in December. Barça won the match 0–1 with a strike outside the area by Andrés Iniesta in the 42nd minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/l-hospitalet-fc-barcelona-once-again-exemplary-0-1|title=Barça debut in the Cup.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=9 November 2011|access-date=10 November 2011}}</ref>

On 22 November, assistant coach Tito Vilanova was successfully operated for problem in his [[parotid gland]]. The club did not release anymore information on the matter due to the coach's wish to have everything remain private.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/tito-vilanova-recovering-after-successful-surgery|title=Tito Villanova successfully operated.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=22 November 2011|access-date=23 November 2011}}</ref> The next day, Barcelona defeated [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] at the [[San Siro]] 2–3 in a thrilling European encounter to win [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group H|Group H]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/champions-league/round-5-h/milan_fc-barcelona|title=Barça win Group H.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=23 November 2011|access-date=28 November 2011}}</ref>

On 26 November, Barça lost its first official match of the season with a 1–0 defeat at Getafe with a goal by [[Juan Valera Espín|Juan Valera]] in the 67th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/getafe-fcb-first-defeat-of-the-season-1-0|title=Barça see 1st defeat.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=27 November 2011|access-date=28 November 2011}}</ref> The defeat leaves Barcelona 6 points behind Real Madrid with 2 matches to go for the first ''[[el Clásico]]'' of the season.

===December===
On 10 December, the first Clásico of the season was contested at the Bernabéu with Barça securing a 1–3 victory over their great rivals. Real Madrid's forward [[Karim Benzema]] scored the fastest goal in Clásico history after getting one past goalkeeper Víctor Valdés off two deflections 24 seconds into the match. Within 30 minutes, Barça equalized with a strike from Alexis followed by a goal by Fàbregas, making it three years running that their big summer transfers score in the first Clásico of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/r-madrid-fc-barcelona-universal-declaration-of-beautiful-football|title=Barça wins first Clásico.|publisher=FCBarcelona.es|date=10 December 2011|access-date=11 December 2011}}</ref>

On 15 December, David Villa [[Bone fracture|fractured]] his [[tibia]] while attempting to score in Barça's 0–4 FIFA Club World Cup semi-final victory over [[Qatar]]i club [[Sadd Sports Club|Al-Sadd]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/mundial-de-clubs/1-2/al-sadd_fc-barcelona|title=Barça into FIFA CWC Final.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=15 December 2011|access-date=15 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111222010340/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/mundial-de-clubs/1-2/al-sadd_fc-barcelona|archive-date=22 December 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> The injury will sideline the player for four-to-six months, possibly causing him to miss [[UEFA Euro 2012]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/david-villa-breaks-shinbone-during-al-sadd-clash|title=Villa sideline with injury..|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=15 December 2011|access-date=15 December 2011}}</ref>

On 18 December, Barcelona claimed the Club World Cup with a 0–4 victory over Brazilian club [[Santos FC|Santos]] in Japan. A brace from Lionel Messi and strikes from Xavi and Fabregas gave Barça their fifth title in 2011 and their second title in this [[FIFA Club World Cup|competition]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/mundial-de-clubs/final/santos_fc-barcelona|title=Barça's crowned Club World Cup champs.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=18 December 2011|access-date=18 December 2011}}</ref>

On 22 December, Barcelona defeated [[CE L'Hospitalet|L'Hospitalet]] in the second leg of the Copa del Rey 9–0<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/copa-del-rei/1-16-tornada/fc-barcelona_l-hospitalet/report |title=Barcelona win big. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=23 December 2011 |access-date=1 January 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120109035711/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/copa-del-rei/1-16-tornada/fc-barcelona_l-hospitalet/report |archive-date=9 January 2012 }}</ref> (10–0 aggregate). Strikes from Pedro, Iniesta, Xavi, [[Thiago Alcântara|Thiago]], [[Cristian Tello]] and [[Isaac Cuenca]] sealed what was another superb display of talent and command on the pitch by the Catalans. The latter three scored a brace each and the win helped the team proceed to the next round of the competition where they face Osasuna at Camp Nou in a first leg Round of 16 tie.

===January===
On 4 January, Barça started off the year with a 4–0 victory over Osasuna in their Round of 16 tie at the Camp Nou.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/copa-del-rei/1-8-anada/fc-barcelona_osasuna |title=Barça takes 1st leg. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=4 January 2012 |access-date=9 January 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107200611/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/copa-del-rei/1-8-anada/fc-barcelona_osasuna |archive-date=7 January 2012 }}</ref> Lionel Messi came off the bench to score two goals in the last 20 minutes after he was left off the team sheet earlier in the day due to the flu.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/01/05/futbol/equipos/barcelona/1325718837.html|title=Messi with the flu still stars for Barça.|work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=5 January 2012|access-date=9 January 2012}}</ref>

On 8 January, the ''[[derbi barceloní]]'' ended in a 1–1 draw with goals by Cesc Fàbregas (16th minute) for Barcelona and [[Álvaro Vázquez]] (86th minute) for [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-18/espanyol_fc-barcelona|title=Stalemate in the Catalan Derby.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=8 January 2012|access-date=2012-01-09}}</ref> Barcelona [[right back]] Dani Alves was racially abused by the Espanyol fans throughout the match and prompted the Espanyol coach [[Mauricio Pochettino]] to "condemn the actions of his fans."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1006359/espanyol-boss-mauricio-pochettino-slams-dani-alves-abuse?cc=5901|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120112042123/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1006359/espanyol-boss-mauricio-pochettino-slams-dani-alves-abuse?cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 January 2012|title=Dani Alves racially abused by Espanyol fans.|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=8 January 2012|access-date=2012-01-09}}</ref>

On 9 January, Lionel Messi was awarded the [[2011 FIFA Ballon d'Or]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/ballondor/news/newsid=1565454/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120109192212/http://www.fifa.com/ballondor/news/newsid=1565454/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 January 2012|title=Messi wins 2011 FIFA Ballon d'Or.|publisher=[[FIFA]]|date=9 January 2012|access-date=10 January 2012}}</ref> and Pep Guardiola received the FIFA Coach of the Year<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/ballondor/news/newsid=1566223/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120112062333/http://www.fifa.com/ballondor/news/newsid=1566223/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 January 2012|title=Guardiola named Coach of the Year.|publisher=[[FIFA]]|date=9 January 2012|access-date=10 January 2012}}</ref> award in [[Zürich]]. With the award, Messi wins his third consecutive Ballon d'Or, joining [[Michel Platini]], [[Marco van Basten]] and [[Johan Cruyff]] as the only three-time winners, and the first since Platini to win it three consecutive years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/ballondor/news/newsid=1566015/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120112061409/http://www.fifa.com/ballondor/news/newsid=1566015/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 January 2012|title=Messi joins Platini, van Basten and Cruyff as 3X winners.|publisher=[[FIFA]]|date=9 January 2012|access-date=2012-01-10}}</ref>

On 11 January, Barça and French club [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] agreed to the transfer of Brazilian [[left back]] [[Maxwell (footballer, born 1981)|Maxwell]] for €4 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/maxwell-transferred-to-paris-saint-germain|title=Maxwell leaves for PSG.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=12 January 2012|access-date=12 January 2012}}</ref>

On 12 January, Barcelona defeated Osasuna 1–2<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.es/futbol/primer-equipo/archivo-partidos/2011-2012/copa-del-rei/1-8-tornada/osasuna_fc-barcelona |title=Barça advance on 6-1 aggregate. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=12 January 2012 |access-date=13 January 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120626230144/http://www.fcbarcelona.es/futbol/primer-equipo/archivo-partidos/2011-2012/copa-del-rei/1-8-tornada/osasuna_fc-barcelona |archive-date=26 June 2012 }}</ref> at the [[Reyno de Navarra Stadium|Reyno de Navarra]] to move on to the Copa del Rey quarter-finals where they'll meet Real Madrid for another round of Clásicos. [[Centre-back|CB]] Andreus Fontàs will miss the rest of the year when he suffered a torn [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in the 14th minute of play.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/andreu-fontas-injured-the-bitter-side-of-the-game|title=Fontàs out for season with torn ACL.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=12 January 2012|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref> Pedro will also be sidelined for ten days due to a minor hamstring injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/pedro-out-for-ten-days|title=Pedro out for 10 days.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=13 January 2012|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref>

On 15 January, Barcelona defeated [[Real Betis]] 4–2 to remain five points back in second place in La Liga table.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-betis-three-vital-points-4-2|title=Barça keep pace.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=15 January 2012|access-date=16 January 2012}}</ref> With the victory, Pep Guardiola notched his 100th win in the Primera División, only needing 132 matches to accomplish the feat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/josep-guardiola-reaches-his-100th-win-in-the-liga-since-he-arrived-in-2008|title=Pep hits century mark in La Liga wins.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=15 January 2012|access-date=16 January 2012}}</ref>

On 18 January, Barça defeated Real Madrid at the Bernabéu in consecutive months, by a 1–2 scoreline. Goals by defenders [[Carles Puyol]] and Eric Abidal secured the comeback victory in the first leg.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/madrid-fc-barcelona-happy-birthday-pep-1-2|title=Barça take 1st leg advantage.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=18 January 2012|access-date=19 January 2012}}</ref> The match did not end without some controversy as Real Madrid's defender [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]] seemed to have stepped on Lionel Messi's hand while the latter was sitting on the ground. The player escaped without sanction from the referee even though the action was viewed by every camera angle at the stadium.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/01/19/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1326956531.html|title=Pepe controversy.|work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=19 January 2012|access-date=19 January 2012}}</ref>

On 22 January, the postponed Week 1 match against [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] due to the player's strike was played at [[La Rosaleda Stadium|La Rosadela]] with Barça taking a 1–4 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/lliga/jornada-1/malaga_fc-barcelona|title=Messi's hat-trick leads Barça.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=22 January 2012|access-date=22 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120121142213/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/lliga/jornada-1/malaga_fc-barcelona|archive-date=21 January 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> A Lionel Messi hat-trick provided all three points for Barcelona to keep pace on Real Madrid for the title.

On 25 January, Barcelona eliminated Real Madrid from the Copa del Rey with a 2–2<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/copa-del-rey/1-8-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_real-madrid |title=Barça into the semis of the CdR. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=25 January 2012 |access-date=25 January 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120128153929/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/copa-del-rey/1-8-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_real-madrid |archive-date=28 January 2012 }}</ref> draw at Camp Nou to win the tie 4–3 on aggregate and reached their 50th semi-final all time in the competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/clasico/barca-jugara-semifinal-1356122|title=Barça in their 50th semi-final.|publisher=Sport.es|language=es|date=26 January 2012|access-date=26 January 2012}}</ref>

On 29 January, Barça were held to a scoreless draw by [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] at the [[Estadio El Madrigal|El Madrigal]] to put them seven points behind league leaders Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/luck-fails-to-reward-commitment-0-0|title=Barça drop 7 points back.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=29 January 2012|access-date=30 January 2012}}</ref> Two days later, Isaac Cuenca extended his contract until 30 June 2015 and was officially promoted to the first-team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/cuenca-signs-extension-to-contract|title=Cuenca promoted.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=31 January 2012|access-date=30 January 2012}}</ref>

===February===
On 8 February, Barcelona defeated [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] 2–0 at Camp Nou and 3–1 on aggregate to advance to their 34th Copa del Rey final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/copa-del-rey/1-2-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_valencia|title=Barça reached CdR Final.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=8 February 2012|access-date=8 February 2012}}</ref> Goals from Cesc Fàbregas and Xavi to set up a rematch of the [[2009 Copa del Rey Final|2009]] final against [[Athletic Bilbao]].

On 11 February, Barcelona suffered their second loss of the season, 3–2 to Osasuna in [[Pamplona]]. With the loss, the team continued to show their struggles in the league away from the Camp Nou, dropping ten points behind leaders Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-23/osasuna_fc-barcelona|title=Barça lose their second on the road.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=11 February 2012|access-date=11 February 2012}}</ref>

On 14 February, Barcelona defeated [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] at the [[BayArena]] with a 3–1 win in their Champions League first leg encounter to move closer to qualifying for the quarter-finals. [[Alexis Sánchez]] scored his first two goals in the Champions League in first start.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/champions-league/1-8-1st-leg/bayer-leverkusen_fc-barcelona|title=Barça take first leg advantage.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=14 February 2012|access-date=20 February 2012}}</ref>

On 19 February, Barcelona notched their 15th win in La Liga against Valencia with a 5–1<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-24/fc-barcelona_valencia|title=Barça stays on pace with Real Madrid.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=19 February 2012|access-date=20 February 2012}}</ref> scoreline at Camp Nou to keep pace with Real Madrid. Lionel Messi celebrated his 200th match in La Liga by scoring four goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-scores-4-goals-to-celebrate-his-200th-game|title=Super Messi scores fur against Valencia.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=19 February 2012|access-date=20 February 2012}}</ref>

On 26 February, Barcelona defeated [[Atlético Madrid]] with a 1–2<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-25/at-madrid_fc-barcelona|title=Barça still in hunt for La Liga.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=26 February 2012|access-date=28 February 2012}}</ref> scoreline at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium|Vicente Calderón]]. Lionel Messi was booked in the eighth minute for a handball and will miss his first match in his career due to cards accumulation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-and-busquets-will-miss-the-match-against-sporting-gijon-due-to-suspension|title=Messi & Sergio to miss Sporting match.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=27 February 2012|access-date=28 February 2012}}</ref>

===March===
On 3 March, Barcelona defeated Sporting Gijón with a 3–1 score despite playing with ten men for more than half-an-hour after Gerard Piqué was sent off for throwing his boot at the Sporting de Gijón kit man at the start of the second half.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-26/fc-barcelona_sporting-de-gijon|title=Barça win despite playing with 10 men.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=3 March 2012|access-date=2012-03-03}}</ref>

On 7 March, Barcelona defeated Bayer Leverkusen 7–1<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/champions-league/1-8-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_bayer-leverkusen|title=Barça smoke Bayer 7-1.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=7 March 2012|access-date=2012-03-07}}</ref> with Lionel Messi becoming the first player to score five goals in a match in the Champions League era. Cristian Tello made a great debut in the competition by scoring his first two goals to complete the Barça rout.

On 11 March, Barcelona defeated [[Racing de Santander]] 0–2 in [[Cantabria]] to notch their 18th win in La Liga. The goals were scored by Lionel Messi to take his season total to 50 goals with more than two months left in the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.es/futbol/primer-equipo/archivo-partidos/2011-2012/liga/jornada-27/racing-de-santander_fc-barcelona|title=Barça keep pace.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=11 March 2012|access-date=2012-03-14}}</ref>

On 15 March, Barcelona announced that defender Eric Abidal will have "a liver transplant as a result of the progress of his liver disease" and will miss the rest of the season. No further information was made available "at the express wish of the player, the club requested the utmost respect for the right to privacy and confidentiality".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/eric-abidal-to-have-a-liver-transplant|title=Abidal to be operated again.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=15 March 2012|access-date=2012-03-15}}</ref>

On 17 March, Barcelona defeated Sevilla 0–2 at the [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium|Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán]]. The first goal was scored off a stunning freekick by Xavi in the 17th minute and the second by Messi in the 24th minute after a great display of team passing.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-28/sevilla_fc-barcelona|title=Barça win Sevilla.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=17 March 2012|access-date=2012-03-17}}</ref>

On 20 March, Barcelona beat Granada 5–3<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-29/fc-barcelona_granada-c-f|title=Barça defeat a valiant Granada.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=20 March 2012|access-date=2012-03-20}}</ref> at Camp Nou behind a historic hat-trick by Lionel Messi. Messi took his career tally to 234 goals as a Barcelona player and surpassed [[César Rodríguez Álvarez|César]] as [[List of FC Barcelona records and statistics#Top scorers in all competitions|the all-time top scorer]] for the club in competitive matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-all-time-top-goalscorer-for-barca-in-official-matches|title=Messi overtakes César.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=20 March 2012|access-date=2012-03-21}}</ref>

On 28 March, Barcelona and Milan finished 0–0 at [[San Siro]] in their first leg quarter-finals encounter in the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/champions-league/1-4-1st-leg/milan_fc-barcelona|title=1st leg draw in QF.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=28 March 2012|access-date=2012-03-28}}</ref> The next day, Barça filed a complaint with [[UEFA]] over the state of the pitch after both clubs agreed it would be in suitable conditions to play.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/barca-present-complaint-about-condition-of-giuseppe-meazza-pitch|title=Barça file complaint over San Siro pitch.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=29 March 2012|access-date=2012-03-30}}</ref> Guardiola said, "it is bad for the spectacle, but to be champions we must overcome all adversities. We have done this many times, although people say otherwise."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1041998/barcelona-lodge-ac-milan-pitch-complaint-to-uefa?cc=5901|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401010853/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1041998/barcelona-lodge-ac-milan-pitch-complaint-to-uefa?cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=1 April 2012|title=Pep talks about pitch.|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=29 March 2012|access-date=2012-03-30}}</ref>

===April===
On 3 April, Barcelona advanced to its fifth consecutive Champions League semi-finals with a 3–1 victory (3–1 on aggregate) over Milan.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/champions-league/1-4-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_milan|title=Barça advance to semi-finals|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=3 April 2012|access-date=2012-04-03}}</ref> Lionel Messi scored two penalties to take his season tally to 14 goals and set a new record in the Champions League era.

On 4 April, Barcelona announced that [[FC Barcelona B|Barcelona B]] defender [[Marc Muniesa]] signed an extension to his contract and will be promoted to the first team for the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/muniesa-s-contract-extension-takes-effect|title=Muniesa promoted to first team.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=4 April 2012|access-date=2012-04-05}}</ref>

On 10 April, Barcelona defeated Getafe 4–0<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-getafe-barca-get-ten-out-of-ten-4-0|title=Victory against Getafe.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=10 April 2012|access-date=2012-04-11}}</ref> at Camp Nou to sleep one point behind league leaders Real Madrid. The victory was dedicated to defender Eric Abidal who underwent a liver transplant, from players and coaches at the post-game press conference.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1047750/eric-abidal-recovering-well-after-liver-transplant?cc=5901|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120714013100/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1047750/eric-abidal-recovering-well-after-liver-transplant?cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 July 2012|title=Victory dedicated to Abidal.|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=11 April 2012|access-date=2012-04-11}}</ref>

On 14 April, Barcelona came back to defeat Levante 1–2 at the [[Estadi Ciutat de València|Ciutat de València]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/llevant-fc-barcelona-confidence-boosting-fightback-1-2|title=Barça comeback victory over Levante.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=14 April 2012|access-date=2012-04-15}}</ref> Lionel Messi lead with a brace and took his tally to 41 goals in the league, that left him tied with Real Madrid's Cristiano Ronaldo for the [[2011–12 La Liga#Awards and season statistics|league lead]]. They also surpassed the record of 40 goals in a season set by Cristiano Ronaldo [[2010–11 La Liga#Awards and season statistics|last season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-it-was-a-very-difficult-ground-to-play-in-but-we-managed-to-get-a-fantastic-result|title=Messi goal scoring feats continues.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=15 April 2012|access-date=2012-04-15}}</ref>

On 18 April, Barcelona lost its first match in this season's Champions League, 1–0 to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] in London. Even though they dominated every aspect of the match, they were defeated at the stroke of half-time by the lone goal scored by [[Didier Drogba]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/chelsea-fc-barcelona-tuesday-set-for-fightback-1-0|title=Shooting boots let down Barça's attack.|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=18 April 2012|access-date=2012-04-19}}</ref>

On 21 April, Barcelona lost their second game in row after being defeated at Camp Nou by fierce rival Real Madrid with a scoreline of 1–2 in ''[[El Clásico]]''. [[Sami Khedira]], Alexis Sánchez and Cristiano Ronaldo provided the goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-35/fc-barcelona_real-madrid|title=Barça fall in the Clásico.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=21 April 2012|access-date=2012-04-24}}</ref>

On 24 April, Barcelona drew 2–2 with Chelsea in the 2nd leg semi-final of the Champions League at the Camp Nou. [[Sergio Busquets]] and Andrés Iniesta put Barcelona up 2–0 by the 44th minute as the Spanish club again dominated possession from the start, owning 73% for the game. In between those goals, Chelsea captain [[John Terry]] was given a straight red card for putting his knee into the back of Alexis Sánchez, as Barcelona seemed well on its way to reach a third final in four years making a Chelsea fightback look even more unlikely. But [[Ramires]] lobbed a shot right before half-time giving the advantage back to his team on aggregate, and the Spanish giants never found a way to recover after the break. After Lionel Messi blasted a penalty off the crossbar in the 59th minute and came close once again with another, Chelsea goalkeeper [[Petr Čech]] making a diving effort to slightly alter the ball's path to the post. Substitute [[Fernando Torres]] dribbled round Víctor Valdés to score in added time to make it 2–3 on aggregate and sealed Barcelona's elimination from Europe.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.es/futbol/primer-equipo/archivo-partidos/2011-2012/champions-league/1-2-vuelta/fc-barcelona_chelsea|title=Barça crash out of Europe.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=24 April 2012|access-date=2012-04-25}}</ref>

On 27 April, manager Pep Guardiola announced he would step down as coach at the end of the season. His record of 13 trophies in four seasons has made him the most successful coach in Barcelona's history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/guardiola-to-leave-barca-on-june-30|title=Pep leaves Barça.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=27 April 2012|access-date=2012-04-27}}</ref> At the press conference in which Barcelona confirmed Guardiola's exit, the team also announced that he would be succeeded by current assistant Tito Vilanova. Vilanova will begin leading the first team at the start of the [[2012–13 FC Barcelona season|2012–13 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Tito Vilanova to be the new manager |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/tito-vilanova-to-be-the-new-manager |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=27 April 2012 |access-date=2012-04-27}}</ref>

===May===
On 2 May, Barcelona defeated Málaga 4–1<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-20/fc-barcelona_malaga|title=Barça defeat Málaga.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=2 May 2012|access-date=2012-05-03}}</ref> at the Camp Nou. Lionel Messi scored a hat-trick and took his season tally to 68 goals in all competitions, passing [[Gerd Müller]]'s record of 67 goals in the [[1972–73 Fußball-Bundesliga|1972–73 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/leo-messi-breaks-muller-s-longstanding-record-of-67-goals-scored-in-one-season|title=Messi breaks season scoring record.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=2 May 2012|access-date=2012-05-03}}</ref>

On 5 May, Barcelona took the second leg of the ''derbi barceloní'' with a 4–0<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-37/fc-barcelona_espanyol|title=Barça defeat Espanyol|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=5 May 2012|access-date=2012-05-07}}</ref> victory over Espanyol. Lionel Messi scored four times and became the first player in La Liga to score 50 goals in a season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-the-perfect-scorer|title=Messi reaches 50 goals.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=7 May 2012|access-date=2012-05-07}}</ref> It was also an emotional farewell match for Guardiola in his last home game as Barça's manager.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/see-you-soon|title=Emotional goodbyes for Pep.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=6 May 2012|access-date=2012-05-07}}</ref>

On 12 May, Barcelona drew their last league game of the season at the [[Estadio Benito Villamarín|Benito Villamarín]] 2–2<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/league/round-38/betis_fc-barcelona|title=Barça finishes season with draw.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=13 May 2012|access-date=2012-05-14}}</ref> against Real Betis. Barça finished 9 points off the league winner Real Madrid while Lionel Messi finished with 50 league goals to win the [[Pichichi Trophy]] and [[European Golden Boot]] as the league's top scorer<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/record-breaking-pichichi-and-golden-boot|title=Messi claims Pichichi & European Golden Boot.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=14 May 2012|access-date=2012-05-14}}</ref> and Víctor Valdés claimed the [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy|Zamora Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/the-zamora-trophy-belongs-to-valdes|title=Valdés claims 4th straight Zamora Trophy.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=14 May 2012|access-date=2012-05-14}}</ref>

On 25 May, Barcelona claimed its 26th Copa del Rey with a 0–3 victory over Athletic Bilbao at the Vicente Calderón in [[Madrid]]. Pedro scored twice while Messi added the third in the seventh final contested between the two teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2011-2012/copa-del-rey/final/athletic-club_fc-barcelona|title=Barça win Copa del Rey.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=25 May 2012|access-date=2012-05-25}}</ref>
